Manor School
A Warm Welcome to Manor School
I am immensely proud to be the Headteacher of Manor School and it is my great pleasure to welcome you to our school website.
Manor School is a large and growing special school located in the London Borough of Brent and is part of The Rise Partnership Trust. We have almost 230 incredible pupils on roll, from Reception to Year 6. We currently have two sites and will be opening a third at the start of the 2026-27 academic year.
The Manor School Early Years Centre (MSEYC) is based on Bridge Road in the Neasden area. Our existing primary site – Manor School Kensal Rise – is approximately two miles away on Chamberlayne Road, and our exciting new site – Manor School Kilburn – will open on Canterbury Road in September 2026.
Our motto is “Love, Learn, Laugh” and this permeates everything that we do. As you will see in our Curriculum Brochure and across other sections of the website, our curriculum offer is well defined, broad, balanced and enriching.
We aim to support our pupils to make the most of their unique potential. We never underestimate a child’s ability and we treasure the close working relationships that we have with our pupils’ families.
Manor School has a reputation for being a centre of excellence. However, despite our successes, we are always striving to be better and we are constantly looking for ways to improve our provision and the lives of our wonderful pupils.
As a school, we are outward facing and passionate about supporting the sector and the work of others. We work in close partnership with a large number of settings and aim to share our knowledge, skills and expertise as widely as we can.
Thank you for taking the time to visit our website. I hope that you find what you are looking for. If not, please do not hesitate to contact the school office.

Our motto: 'Love, Learn, Laugh', underpins everything we do.

Partnerships
Challenge Partners Hub
Manor School is an active member of the Challenge Partners Shared Horizons Hub, working collaboratively with other schools to share expertise, develop leadership and improve teaching and learning. The Hub provides opportunities for professional development, peer learning and joint school improvement across the partnership.
Challenge Partners
Challenge Partners is a national network supporting schools to improve through collaboration, professional development and the sharing of effective practice. Through the wider network, Manor School has opportunities to learn from and contribute to schools and education professionals across the country. Challenge Partners
BHHAG
The Brent, Harrow and Hertfordshire Assessment Group (BHHAG) brings together specialist schools to share expertise and develop approaches to assessment, curriculum and preparing pupils for adulthood. Manor contributes to collaborative work, evidence-based practice and the development of high-quality provision for pupils with complex needs.
BSP
The Brent Schools Partnership (BSP) brings schools across Brent together to share expertise and support school improvement. Through its Partners for Excellence programme, Manor benefits from specialist support, professional development and opportunities to share and develop effective practice with other schools.
BANG
BANG is a Brent-based charity working with young people and communities through creative, educational and wellbeing-focused programmes. Manor works closely with BANG to provide pupils with inclusive opportunities including creative activities, drumming, movement and outdoor learning, supporting personal development, confidence and community connection.

Curriculum Offer
Our Manor School Curriculum is designed to help our pupils to RISE so they can be Resilient, Independent, Skilled, Expressive. This section of the website gives a brief overview of the curriculum and content. Further information can be found in the Curriculum Brochure which can be downloaded below.
Pupils at Manor School follow an adapted version of the National Curriculum. Each half-term, year groups have a new planning theme to help support pupils’ progression and learning. Each theme is taught in a cross-curricular manner and builds on the subject knowledge of the themes that come before it. The curriculum is well-sequenced and there is a specific focus on supporting pupils to develop knowledge, skills and key vocabulary over time so that they know more, remember more and are able to do more.

EYFS Curriculum
At Manor School, we recognise our obligation to follow the SEND Code of Practice and honour the Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) of every pupil. Pupils entering Manor School in Reception start in our EYFS provision. This follows the EYFS statutory framework.
Learning and Development requirements comprise the seven areas of learning:
A particular focus on the three prime areas is key; the four specific areas are then used to strengthen and apply learning in the prime areas. Moreover, the four Outcome Areas of each pupil’s EHCP and strongly interconnected with the EYFS Prime and Specific areas of learning; by viewing the EYFS areas of learning and development through the lens of each pupil’s EHCP we will be providing for the best possible outcomes.
The Seven Features of Effective Practice (Development Matters 2021) are embedded in our approach to quality-first teaching:
Development Matters informs planning where appropriate, but we aim to prioritise pupils’ needs according to the EHCPs. Development Matters statements support assessment through the EYFS Profile; this is used alongside our bespoke and robust developmental assessment system Small Steps, which incorporates relevant content from a range of sources, including Development Matters.
The Long Term Planners for EYFS follow our “Ready, Steady, Go!” Curriculum which aims to develop pupils readiness for learning in the Autumn Term, ensure that they are on a steady path of progression in the Spring term and then use the Summer Term to prepare them to “Go” to Key Stage One. Unit Planners are available which help identify key skills in each term and to help make clear the links between the EHCP outcomes and the seven areas of learning. In addition to working on the seven areas of learning every day at the Manor School Early Years site pupils also have the opportunity to visit the Manor School Main site once a week to undertake PE, Swimming and Art sessions. This further broadens their learning opportunities, allows them access to additional facilities and supports pupils in becoming familiar with the main school site which aids their transition to Key Stage One.

At Manor School, we aspire for all our pupils to engage in subject-specific learning based on National Curriculum subject areas. Each subject area has its own intent statement, setting out a clear vision of the importance of learning in each area. Equality, Diversity and Inclusion
At Manor School, we are dedicated to nurturing diverse and inclusive communities where our pupils and staff are able to thrive and fulfil their full potential.
At Rise Partnership Trust we serve pupils with SEND and understand inclusion underpins everything we do. We are driven by our core values love, learn and laugh and believe that every pupil deserves an education that is right for them and pride ourselves on creating a bespoke curriculum that meets each pupils’ needs, interests and aspirations.
We are committed to achieving equality, diversity and inclusion amongst our staff and community by promoting and celebrating diversity.
